paragraphs: Swamiji compared the hold nature has on us to a little scene. A Frenchman invited an English friend to his home and boasted about the old wines stored in his cellar. He sent for a bottle of his finest vintage. It looked gorgeous, with light glinting inside it like a piece of gold. The butler filled a glass, and the Englishman calmly drank it down.
Only then did it come out: the butler had brought a bottle of castor oil.
That, said Swamiji, is our condition. Nature hands us castor oil dressed up as golden wine, and we keep drinking it, all the time, without being able to stop.
learn: Plenty of things look golden and turn out bitter: the endless scroll, the shortcut, the flattering crowd. Before you swallow something because it looks attractive, check what is really in the bottle.
